title: Telemetry contract adapter: SDK/CLI/API compatibility shim and pipeline migration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a compatibility-first telemetry contract adapter that lets SDKs, the CLI, and internal API clients emit telemetry while the backend analytics pipeline migrates to the new normalized event contract. The goal is zero customer-visible breakage during backend ingestion changes and to provide a plan for incremental rollout, visibility, and rollback.

Scope:
- Add a lightweight telemetry handshake endpoint on the console backend so clients can detect supported telemetry feature flags (enriched fields, new event names, schema version token).
- Ship SDK/CLI compatibility shims that: detect server capabilities, emit both v1 and transitional v2 fields where necessary, and gate experimental keys behind flags.
- Implement ingestion-layer adapter transform that accepts v1 and v2 payloads, normalizes them into canonical internal schema, and annotates events with origin_version for migration analytics.
- Update Kafka topics / schema registry rules and create a read-model migration for the analytics warehouse to pick up canonical events.
- Rollout plan with canary traffic, health checks, and automatic fallback to old ingestion path on errors.

Success criteria / Acceptance:
1) No increase in client-side errors (SDK/CLI) after enabling the new ingestion adapter during canary.
2) >=95% of incoming events are correctly normalized within 10 minutes of ingest during canary.
3) Clear dashboards showing origin_version distribution, normalization error rate, and event latency.
4) SDK/CLI tests include golden payloads and round-trip integration tests against a staging ingestion adapter.

Design decisions made so far:
- Use a /telemetry/capabilities API returning a short JSON with supported_fields and schema_token to avoid embedding version in every event header. This keeps overhead low and enables feature flagging per-client.
- Emit both legacy and normalized fields from SDKs for a 4-week overlap window, then switch to normalized-only once pipelines and consumers validate.
- Ingestion adapter will run as a stateless microservice in front of the Kafka producer; errors will be idempotent and routed to a dead-letter topic for inspection.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Spike in traffic parsing costs due to dual-emission. Mitigation: enable prefix-based sampling and increase canary throttles; the handshake will allow clients to stop dual emission early if backend signals readiness.
- Risk: Consumers relying on legacy fields may break. Mitigation: communicate timeline, add feature-flagged consumer compatibility layer and a consumer migration checklist.

Operational checklist for rollout:
- Create canary cohort: 5% of production tokens routed to new adapter.
- Enable verbose telemetry for canary clients.
- Monitor normalization_error_rate, event_processing_latency_95p, and consumer_backpressure.
- If normalization_error_rate > 1% for 30m, auto-fallback to legacy pipeline and create incident ticket.

Artifacts and links:
- Telemetry contract doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TELEMETRY/Contract-Adapter-Design
- Draft SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2142
- Ingestion adapter prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-adapter/tree/telemetry-adapter

Next steps:
1) Finalize handshake API spec and add to openapi.yaml (owner: Backend API).
2) Land SDK compatibility PR with integration tests against staging adapter (owner: SDK team).
3) Deploy ingestion adapter to staging, run end-to-end validation with sample workloads (owner: Observability).
4) Schedule canary and make decision to migrate after 2 business days of stable metrics.
